identity.title: The ALMA Survey of 70 μm Dark High-mass Clumps in Early Stages (ASHES). X. Hot Gas Reveals Deeply Embedded Star Formation

paper_type_evidence.quote: We have carried out the pilot Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) Survey of 70 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$ dark High-mass clumps in Early Stages (ASHES) toward 12 IRDC clumps.

question.value: Kinetic temperatures and embedded star-formation activity in 12 70 μm dark IRDCs

evidence.quote: At a scale of about 5000 au using formaldehyde (H$_2$CO) emission, we investigate the kinetic temperature of dense cores in 12 IRDCs obtained from the pilot ALMA Survey of 70 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$ dark High-mass clumps in Early Stages (ASHES).

Observations of twelve 70 $\mu$m IRDC clumps were performed with ALMA in Band 6 ($\sim$224 GHz; 1.34 mm) using the main 12 m array, the 7 m array, and the total power (TP) array (Project ID: 2015.1.01539.S, PI: P. Sanhueza).

Observations of twelve 70 $\mu$m IRDC clumps were performed with ALMA in Band 6 ($\sim$224 GHz; 1.34 mm) using the main 12 m array, the 7 m array, and the total power (TP) array (Project ID: 2015.1.01539.S, PI: P. Sanhueza).
HC$_3$N $J$ = 24-23 (hereafter, HC$_3$N(24-23)) with $E_u/k$ = 130 K
OCS $J$ =18-17 (hereafter, OSC(18-17)) with $E_u/k$ = 100 K
We note that some cores also have c-C$_3$H$_2$ $J_{K_AK_C}$ = $5_{1,4}-4_{2,3}$ ($E_u/k$ = 35.4 K), which can trace outflow cavities (cite: Tychoniec2021).
Figure [8](#dv-relation) presents the relation between the velocity dispersion of C$^{18}$O(2-1) ($\sigma_{\rm C^{18}O}$) and H$_2$CO ($\sigma_{\rm H_2CO(3_{0,3}-2_{0,2})}$) for cores and pixels.

claims.hypothesis: H2CO traces quiescent dense gas in early-stage IRDCs
claims.experiment: Compare H2CO spatial distributions, linewidths, and wings with continuum, C18O, and CO outflows
claims.result: H2CO differs from continuum and its blue/red directions roughly agree with CO outflows
claims.finding: H2CO mainly traces low-velocity outflow components rather than quiescent gas

evidence.quote: The spatial distributions of all H$_2$CO transition lines differ from the material traced by the 1.3 mm dust continuum emission.

The direction of the blue- and red-shifted components roughly agrees with these components detected in CO emission that is considered to trace molecular outflows, as investigated by (cite: Li2020) in the ASHES survey.
We confirmed that H$_2$CO mainly traces the low-velocity outflow components rather than the quiescent gas in the early phase of high-mass star formation.

evidence.quote: Among IRDCs, those that are 70 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$ dark are especially important because they are the coldest, most quiescent clouds (cite: Guzman2015).
From the above, the three transitions of H$_2$CO allow us to probe the kinetic temperature of IRDCs and unveil potential precursors of future massive hot cores.

why_this_method.value: H2CO ladder populations are collisionally controlled; use two temperature methods and matched-resolution NH3 comparisons

evidence.quote: Since the relative population of the $K_a$ ladders of H$_2$CO are almost exclusively determined by collisional processes (cite: Mangum1993), the line ratios involving different $K_a$ ladders are good tracers of the kinetic temperatures (cite: Mangum1993; Muhle2007).

We derived the kinetic temperature of the molecular gas in the IRDC clumps traced by H$_2$CO lines using two methods: (1) under the assumption of local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and (2) with the RADEX non-LTE modeling program (cite: Vandertak2007).

referee_caveats_inferred: The three-line 5σ selection favors bright, excited gas; temperature statistics do not describe all 294 cores.
The RADEX methods specify the 3_2,1–2_2,0 ratio, but the LTE/RADEX comparison attributes a difference to the 3_2,2–2_2,1 ratio; resolve this before reproduction.
The stated LTE linewidth range of 0.14–1.37 km s^-1 is difficult to reconcile with the broader reported core dispersions; clarify its meaning.
The Mach-number subsection reports different ranges and means from the preceding thermal-motion section without clearly identifying the population change.
Pixels re-binned to half a beam remain spatially correlated, which matters for correlation significance.
Temperature and derived non-thermal dispersion share fitted inputs; their correlation is not an independent heating diagnostic.
Outflow-edge shocks and hot-core precursors remain interpretations rather than uniquely established mechanisms.
Exact imaging and manual velocity selections require earlier papers or unreleased task-specific artifacts.
